raw_graphql_pull_request.body:
## Purpose

Granite 4.2 emits tool calls in an XML format:

```
<tool_call>
<function=func_name>
<parameter=key>value</parameter>
</function>
</tool_call>
```

This PR adds a dedicated `granite_toolcall_parser` so Granite 4.2 ships with its own
tool-call parser name.

```bash
vllm serve ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b \
    --tool-call-parser granite_toolcall_parser \
    --enable-auto-tool-choice
```

## Design

`GraniteToolCallParser` is a thin subclass of the existing `GraniteThinkingParser`. Granite 4.2
already drives both `<think>`/`</think>` reasoning and `<tool_call>` XML tool calls through a
single engine, so the subclass inherits the grammar, argument converter and streaming logic
unchanged and is exposed as a standalone `--tool-call-parser`.

- **No duplicated grammar** — the tool-call extraction is inherited, so future fixes to the shared
  parser engine flow in automatically.
- **Works standalone** — it extracts tool calls correctly whether or not
  `--reasoning-parser granite_thinking_parser` is also configured, and with any reasoning parser.
- **Both thinking modes** — behaves identically with `enable_thinking` on and off.

Changes:

- `vllm/parser/granite_toolcall.py` — `GraniteToolCallParser(GraniteThinkingParser)`
- `vllm/tool_parsers/granite_toolcall_parser.py` — tool-parser adapter shim
- `vllm/parser/engine/registered_adapters.py` — generate the adapters
- `vllm/tool_parsers/__init__.py` — register the `granite_toolcall_parser` key
- `docs/features/tool_calling.md` — document the Granite 4.2 row
- `tests/tool_parsers/test_granite_toolcall_parser.py` — parity test suite

## Test Plan

`tests/tool_parsers/test_granite_toolcall_parser.py` runs a shared corpus of model outputs through
both `granite_toolcall_parser` and the in-tree `qwen3_coder` parser (which handles the same XML
format) and asserts byte-identical results. Coverage:

- single / parallel / no-call / reasoning-then-call outputs
- every JSON argument type (int, float, bool, null, string, array, object)
- empty arguments, escaped strings, multiline values, whitespace inside tags
- malformed/partial inputs (missing closing tags, missing `>` on the function name, unclosed
  function names, consecutive calls without a closing tag)
- each case run in non-streaming, per-token streaming, and random-chunk streaming
- each case run with `enable_thinking` both `True` and `False`
- a standalone test confirming extraction works with no reasoning parser configured

## Test Result

```
tests/tool_parsers/test_granite_toolcall_parser.py  212 passed
tests/tool_parsers/test_qwen3coder_tool_parser.py    60 passed
```

## Claude Code Review

This pull request is from a fork — automated review is disabled. A repository maintainer can comment `@claude review` to run a one-time review.

Thanks for the PR. I think the Granite-named flag is fine to add, but the shape is bigger than it needs to be.

Granite 4.2 emits the same tool-call XML as Qwen3-Coder, and this PR shows that: the new class is empty and the parity tests pass because `qwen3_coder` already handles the format. So the parser is really an alias, and an alias does not need a new parser module, a new engine config, a second adapter pair, or a 500-line parity suite.

Subclassing `GraniteThinkingParser` also pulls the leading-newline strip into the tool path. That strip exists to clean up the chat template's newline after `</think>`. When the parser runs on its own with no reasoning parser, it changes plain content (for example `\n\nHello` becomes `Hello`) where `qwen3_coder` keeps it. The test corpus has no leading-newline case, so the parity tests do not catch this.

Suggestion: keep the `granite_toolcall_parser` name or anything that is preferred, but make it a registry alias that maps to `Qwen3EngineToolParser` in `vllm/tool_parsers/__init__.py`, the same way `qwen3` maps to `hermes` today. Then drop `vllm/parser/granite_toolcall.py`, the `registered_adapters.py` hunk, and the parity test file. One small test that the name resolves to the Qwen3 class is enough.

+

@@ -0,0 +1,131 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+import json
+
+import pytest
+
+from tests.tool_parsers.common_tests import ToolParserTestConfig, ToolParserTests
+from tests.tool_parsers.utils import run_tool_extraction
+from vllm.entrypoints.openai.chat_completion.protocol import ChatCompletionRequest
+from vllm.tokenizers import TokenizerLike, get_tokenizer
+from vllm.tool_parsers import ToolParserManager
+
+MODEL = "ibm-granite/granite-4.2-8b"
+
+
+def _tool_call(name: str, params: dict[str, str]) -> str:
+    body = "".join(f"<parameter={k}>\n{v}\n</parameter>\n" for k, v in params.items())
+    return f"<tool_call>\n<function={name}>\n{body}</function>\n</tool_call>"
+
+
+# Granite 4.2 uses its own tokenizer (not gpt2) so special-token boundaries
+# match production. get_tokenizer fetches only the small tokenizer files, not
+# the model weights.
+@pytest.fixture(scope="module")
+def granite_tokenizer() -> TokenizerLike:
+    return get_tokenizer(tokenizer_name=MODEL)
+
+
+class TestGraniteToolCallParser(ToolParserTests):
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def test_config(self) -> ToolParserTestConfig:
+        return ToolParserTestConfig(
+            parser_name="granite_toolcall_parser",
+            no_tool_calls_output="This is a regular response without any tool calls.",
+            single_tool_call_output=_tool_call("get_weather", {"city": "Tokyo"}),
+            parallel_tool_calls_output=(
+                _tool_call("get_weather", {"city": "Tokyo"})
+                + "\n"
+                + _tool_call("get_time", {"timezone": "Asia/Tokyo"})
+            ),
+            various_data_types_output=_tool_call(
+                "test_function",
+                {
+                    "string_field": "hello",
+                    "int_field": "42",
+                    "float_field": "3.14",
+                    "bool_field": "true",
+                    "null_field": "null",
+                    "array_field": '["a", "b", "c"]',
+                    "object_field": '{"nested": "value"}',
+                },
+            ),
+            empty_arguments_output="<tool_call>\n<function=refresh>\n</function>\n</tool_call>",
+            surrounding_text_output=(
+                "Let me check the weather for you."
+                + _tool_call("get_weather", {"city": "Tokyo"})
+            ),
+            escaped_strings_output=_tool_call(
+                "test_function",
+                {
+                    "quoted": 'He said "hello"',
+                    "path": "C:\\Users\\file.txt",
+                    "newline": "line1\nline2",
+                },
+            ),
+            malformed_input_outputs=[
+                # bare opener, never completed
+                "<tool_call>\n<function=",
+                # stray closing tags with no opener
+                "</parameter>\n</function>\n</tool_call>",
+                # tool-call markup embedded in plain prose, no function tag
+                "Here is some text mentioning <tool_call> inline but not a call.",
+            ],
+            single_tool_call_expected_name="get_weather",
+            single_tool_call_expected_args={"city": "Tokyo"},
+            single_tool_call_expected_content=None,
+            parallel_tool_calls_count=2,
+            parallel_tool_calls_names=["get_weather", "get_time"],
+            # Values are typed only when the request carries the tool's JSON
+            # schema; the shared harness builds the parser with no tools, so
+            # every <parameter> value stays a string (same as qwen3_coder).
+            supports_typed_arguments=False,
+        )
+
+    # Granite 4.2 uses its own tokenizer (not gpt2) so special-token
+    # boundaries match production. get_tokenizer fetches only the small
+    # tokenizer files, not the model weights.
+    @pytest.fixture
+    def tokenizer(self, granite_tokenizer: TokenizerLike) -> TokenizerLike:
+        return granite_tokenizer
+
+    # --- Granite-specific tests ---
+
+    @pytest.mark.parametrize("streaming", [True, False])
+    def test_leading_newline_content_preserved(self, tokenizer, streaming):
+        """A standalone tool parser must leave content untouched, matching
+        qwen3_coder. Regression guard: an earlier version subclassed the
+        reasoning parser and stripped the leading newline off plain content.
+        """
+        model_output = "\n\nHello, how can I help you today?"
+        granite = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("granite_toolcall_parser")(
+            tokenizer
+        )
+        qwen = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("qwen3_coder")(tokenizer)
+        g_content, g_calls = run_tool_extraction(
+            granite, model_output, streaming=streaming
+        )
+        q_content, q_calls = run_tool_extraction(
+            qwen, model_output, streaming=streaming
+        )
+        assert g_content == q_content == model_output
+        assert g_calls == q_calls == []
+
+    def test_works_without_reasoning_parser(self, tokenizer):
+        """Reasoning markup with no reasoning parser configured: the tool call
+        is still extracted and the <think> block stays in content verbatim.
+        """
+        model_output = "<think>\nThe user wants the weather.\n</think>\n" + _tool_call(
+            "get_weather", {"city": "Tokyo"}
+        )
+        parser = ToolParserManager.get_tool_parser("granite_toolcall_parser")(tokenizer)
+        request = ChatCompletionRequest(model="test-model", messages=[])
+        extracted = parser.extract_tool_calls(model_output, request=request)
+        assert extracted.tools_called
+        assert len(extracted.tool_calls) == 1
+        assert extracted.tool_calls[0].function.name == "get_weather"
+        assert json.loads(extracted.tool_calls[0].function.arguments) == {
+            "city": "Tokyo"
+        }
+        assert "<think>" in (extracted.content or "")

+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+"""Granite 4.2 tool-call parser.
+
+Granite 4.2 emits tool calls in an XML format::
+
+    <tool_call>
+    <function=func_name>
+    <parameter=key>value</parameter>
+    </function>
+    </tool_call>
+
+Granite 4.2 shares the Nemotron V3 tool-call and reasoning format, so this
+parser subclasses :class:`NemotronV3Parser` to reuse its grammar, argument
+converter and streaming logic, exposed as a standalone ``--tool-call-parser``.
+
+It deliberately does NOT subclass :class:`GraniteThinkingParser`: that parser
+strips a leading newline from content (to clean up the chat template's
+``\\n</think>\\n`` markup), which is a reasoning-side concern. A tool parser
+running on its own (no reasoning parser) must leave content untouched, so the
+leading-newline handling stays in the reasoning parser where it belongs.
+
+Because the tool-call extraction is inherited unchanged, fixes to the shared
+grammar flow in automatically. The parser works on its own, with any reasoning
+parser, or with none, in both thinking modes.
+"""
+
+from __future__ import annotations
+
+from vllm.parser.nemotron_v3 import NemotronV3Parser
+
+
+class GraniteToolCallParser(NemotronV3Parser):
+    """Granite 4.2 tool-call parser.
+
+    Subclass of :class:`NemotronV3Parser` (whose tool-call and reasoning format
+    Granite 4.2 shares) exposed as a standalone tool parser. The tool adapter
+    generated from this class extracts tool calls through the shared grammar;
+    reasoning/content splitting, when enabled, is handled by the separately
+    configured reasoning parser.
+    """

@@ -0,0 +1,11 @@
+# SPDX-License-Identifier: Apache-2.0
+# SPDX-FileCopyrightText: Copyright contributors to the vLLM project
+
+from vllm.parser.engine.registered_adapters import GraniteToolCallParserToolAdapter
+
+
+class GraniteToolCallToolParser(GraniteToolCallParserToolAdapter):  # type: ignore[valid-type, misc]
+    # Structural-tag model whose grammar matches Granite 4.2's XML tool-call
+    # format; one of the keys in SUPPORTED_STRUCTURAL_TAG_MODELS. Only consulted
+    # under VLLM_ENFORCE_STRICT_TOOL_CALLING.
+    structural_tag_model = "qwen_3_coder"
